summary: Learn disaster risk financing, parametric insurance, and layered coverage planning. Build practical tools for resilience and recovery.
lede: The Insurance and Risk Financing Mechanisms for Disasters course helps you decide which losses to retain, transfer, or finance through a structured approach to risk layering, exposure analysis, and liquidity planning. You will learn to compare reserves, contingent credit, insurance, reinsurance, and risk pools within constrained budgets. Through practical scenarios, you will build a risk financing matrix, compare indemnity and parametric insurance, and develop claims and payout workflows. The course also introduces catastrophe bonds, insurance-linked securities, and public-private risk pooling so you can shape an implementable strategy that accounts for affordability, basis risk, timing, and governance.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who need to choose, structure, and defend disaster financing options in real organizational settings.
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of disaster risk management, insurance concepts, or public finance processes. Familiarity with risk assessment, budgeting, or contingency planning is helpful, but no actuarial background is required. The course is designed at an intermediate level, and you will benefit most if you can bring a current or recent example of a disaster recovery funding challenge, insurance gap, reserve policy, or financing proposal from your organization. Coding is not required, and advanced concepts such as catastrophe bonds and parametric triggers are taught at operational awareness level rather than engineering depth.
